title: observability: add token-level cost & latency tracing, per-route dashboards, and alert tuning
author: Aisha Raman
description:
Context: We need finer-grained observability for inference request economics and latency. Customers and platform teams have asked for token-level cost and latency breakdowns per-route and per-model to surface regressions, optimize batching/quantization tradeoffs, and drive SLO-aware routing decisions. This PR instruments token-level metrics and traces, adds a set of Grafana dashboards for per-route token cost/latency breakdowns, and introduces tuned alert rules for cost/latency spikes.

Changeset summary:
- Add token-level counters and histograms in the runtime (token_count, token_processing_ms, token_cost_usd) and emit route/model tags for aggregation. Uses existing OpenTelemetry exporter pipeline so traces link to metrics.
- Wire token-level aggregation into our metrics pipeline (Prometheus metrics + OTLP metrics export).
- New Grafana dashboards: per-route token cost breakdown, percentile token-latency heatmaps, and cross-region cost comparison.
- Alert tuning: alert rules for sudden token-cost-per-minute increases, p99 token latency regressions, and increased model-serving tail latency. Alerts include runbook links and a cooldown window to reduce noise.
- Console: add a per-route metrics view that surfaces token breakdown and cost attribution over time (UI: small chart + top contributing prompts).
- Docs and runbooks updated with instrumentation notes and a short migration guide for existing dashboards.

Motivation: Token-level visibility lets us answer questions like: which routes drive token spend, are recent model rollouts increasing per-token processing time, and where batching/caching changes changed cost-per-token. These are critical for Optimize and for SRE capacity planning.

Checklist: 
- [x] Instrumentation added and unit-tested
- [x] Integration tests validating metric labels and sample rates
- [x] New dashboards reviewed with SRE and Product
- [x] Alerts tuned and validated in canary
- [x] Docs + console UX reviewed

Testing & rollout: Deploy to staging and canary clusters with metrics/trace exporters enabled for 72h. Verified dashboards show expected aggregates and trace linking. Alert thresholds tuned on historical 30d baseline. Rollout is feature-flagged; UI surface behind "token_observability" feature flag.

Risks & rollback: Low-medium. Risk of increased cardinality in Prometheus if callers add high-cardinality tags. Mitigation: we only emit route, model, region, and role tags; high-cardinality prompt hashes are not surfaced. If metrics cardinality grows, immediate rollback path is to disable token counters via feature flag and remove dashboard alerts.

Related: ENG-1420 (token observability baseline), ENG-1453 (console per-route metrics), ref: Linear ENG-1420, ENG-1453.

Notes: This description is intentionally compact; see commits and changed_files for details.

review_comments: Marco Hsu: Can we avoid high-cardinality in label sets? Please confirm the exact labels being emitted.
Author (Aisha): We limit labels to route, model, region, and role. Prompt/content hashes are explicitly not emitted. Added unit tests to assert label set size.
Lena Ortiz: Alert thresholds look noisy on staging when traffic spikes; suggest increasing cooldown to 15m for cost alerts.
Author (Aisha): Increased cooldown to 15m and added a 10m sliding window for evaluation. Reran canary; alerts stabilised.
Priya Kapoor: UX looks good; consider adding a small 'top prompts' table for debugging (feature-flagged).
Author (Aisha): Added a feature-flagged top-prompts table that shows redacted prompt snippets and contribution to token spend (redaction to reduce PII).
release_notes: Added token-level observability: new metrics (token_count, token_processing_ms, token_cost_usd), Grafana dashboards (per-route token cost/latency), tuned alerts for token cost and p99 latency, and a console per-route view behind feature flag. Impact: better cost attribution and faster regression detection.
